subject.title: [Bug]: Codex app-server session wedges indefinitely after a 429 rate-limit burst — terminal-idle watchdog still gated by `activeAppServerTurnRequests > 0` (regression/incomplete fix of #82681)

question: Is structural source/test proof from the merged run-lifecycle stack enough to close this rate-limit-triggered Codex shared-client wedge now, or should closure wait for live 429 confirmation on a release build?
rationale: The latest human issue comment says the failure mode should be structurally retired but explicitly keeps it pending live 429 confirmation, and current main deliberately rejects part of the requested fix shape by retaining the request gate and keeping the terminal timeout internal.

options.title: Wait for release proof
options.body: Keep the issue open until a build containing the run-lifecycle stack is exercised against the reported 429/shared-client wedge or new logs show the remaining failure.

options.title: Close from structural proof
options.body: Close as implemented on main if maintainers decide the current source, tests, and PR provenance are sufficient without live 429 reproduction.

options.title: Reopen fix design
options.body: Queue implementation only if fresh evidence shows current main still wedges multiple co-leased sessions beyond the intended liveness windows.

recommendation.title: Wait for release proof
recommendation.body: Keep the issue open until a build containing the run-lifecycle stack is exercised against the reported 429/shared-client wedge or new logs show the remaining failure.

likelyOwner.reason: obviyus authored and commented on the run-lifecycle work that is the current candidate fix for this issue.
